title: Brewers Plan Friday Parade and Rally in Milwaukee After First World Series Title
dek: The Brewers will parade through downtown Milwaukee at 10 a.m. Friday, then hold a championship rally and fan festival at the Summerfest grounds, following their 4-1 Game 5 win over the Rays.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: American Family Field, the Brewers' home ballpark in Milwaukee, seen from Interstate 94

keyPoints: The Brewers' championship parade starts at 10 a.m. Friday at N. 4th Street and W. Wisconsin Avenue and runs through downtown Milwaukee.
The route ends at Henry Maier Festival Park, where a championship rally and fan festival will be held; the grounds open to the public at 8 a.m. with free general admission until capacity.
Seats in the American Family Insurance Amphitheater for the rally speeches go on sale Thursday, with staggered member presales starting at 10 a.m. and public sales at 2 p.m.
The Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 on Wednesday night in St. Petersburg, Florida, for the first World Series title in franchise history.
body:
The Milwaukee Brewers will hold a championship parade through downtown Milwaukee at 10 a.m. Friday, Oct. 30, the team and local outlets said, a day after the club won its first World Series title with a 4-1 Game 5 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field.

## Route and schedule

The parade begins at the intersection of N. 4th Street and W. Wisconsin Avenue and travels through downtown before ending at Henry Maier Festival Park, according to a team announcement reported by FOX 11. A championship rally and fan festival will follow on the Summerfest grounds.

The festival grounds open to the public at 8 a.m. Friday. Admission to the general grounds is free until capacity is reached. The Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reported that the parade is set for Friday at 10 a.m. and that the team's fans should check brewers.com/Parade for updates.

## Tickets for the rally

Fans who want seats for the rally speeches in the American Family Insurance Amphitheater can buy them beginning Thursday. Staggered presales for season ticket members start at 10 a.m., with public sales opening at 2 p.m. Net proceeds from amphitheater ticket sales will benefit the Brewers Community Foundation, FOX 11 reported. Fans without tickets can watch the speeches on video boards across the grounds.

## The series that ended in St. Petersburg

Milwaukee closed out the series on Wednesday night, one night after Tampa Bay forced Game 5 with a 4-3 win in 12 innings. The Brewers had led the series 3-1 before that game. FOX 11 noted that this was the first World Series since 1991 between teams in the bottom half of payrolls.

## What comes next

Meridian will update this story if the team announces changes to the route, the rally program or ticketing. Fans should follow official Brewers channels and local police and city notices for road closures on game-day logistics.
